title: Lena and the Gravity
premise: Elodie Nakamura smuggles forbidden memories through the orbital ring above Meridian, a dying colony Earth abandoned decades ago. When she intercepts a distress signal in Old Terran—a language extinct since the Severance—she discovers it comes from the gravity well itself, where a hidden generation ship of colonists' descendants has survived, and its message could either end or ignite the war between Meridian's surface survivors and Earth's returning fleet. Carrying the message means betraying the smuggler syndicate that raised her; destroying it means dooming the ship's children to drift forever. Elodie chooses to broadcast it during Earth's final transmission loop, forcing both sides to hear their shared history at once—and in the aftermath, she trades her own memories as payment for the ceasefire, becoming the colony's living archive.
about_author: Isandro Sterling is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals before turning to fiction. They live somewhere with unreliable internet and write about people who carry other people's pasts for a living.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Heart
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. She runs a memory-chip shipment past orbital customs, hiding grief-recordings inside her own neural cache. We learn Meridian is dying—air scrubbers failing, Earth silent for years. The emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness, and the first flicker of guilt over what she profits from carrying.

chapters.title: The Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. A distress signal arrives encoded in Old Terran, extinct since the Severance. Her client, archivist Tomas Reyes, recognizes it and is murdered within hours. Elodie escapes with the only copy. Emotional beat: fear hardening into resolve—the moment the smuggler becomes the message-bearer.

chapters.title: What the Syndicate Owns
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. The Voss syndicate, which raised her, demands the signal; its boss, Maren Voss, reveals Earth's fleet is inbound and the signal proves someone else survived downwell. Elodie stalls, lying badly. Emotional beat: the sick recognition that family was always a debt structure.

chapters.title: Gravity Well
chapters.summary: POV Elodie, descending toward the source coordinates. She finds the derelict entrance to a buried launch site and meets Iyo, a child of the hidden generation ship, who speaks fluent Old Terran. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into horror—Iyo's people have been listening to Meridian die for forty years, unable to answer.

chapters.title: The Ship That Waited
chapters.summary: POV alternating Elodie/Iyo. Inside the ship, Elodie learns the founders sealed it deliberately, hoarding fuel and truth while the surface burned. The council wants silence; a faction wants to broadcast. Emotional beat: inheritance as a cage—children paying for ancestors' cowardice.

chapters.title: Earth Answers
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Earth's fleet arrives early and begins jamming all bands; Maren Voss sells the signal's existence to the fleet commander to save herself. Elodie realizes the message must be sent during the fleet's final transmission loop—a window of ninety seconds. Emotional beat: claustrophobic urgency, allies shrinking.

chapters.title: Ninety Seconds
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. She infiltrates the orbital relay with Iyo and a defected syndicate tech while Voss's hunters close in. The chapter is one continuous countdown: sabotage, betrayal, a sacrifice by the tech. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into clarity—she finally knows what she's willing to lose.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. She sends the message—two centuries of shared history, the ship's confession and plea—into both fleets' open channels. The fleet hesitates; Meridian's surface militias stand down mid-assault. But Voss triggers a counter-transmission framing the ship as an invasion force. Emotional beat: triumph snatched back at the threshold.

chapters.title: The Price of the Loop
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. To override Voss, Elodie offers the relay her own memory cache as verification bandwidth—every smuggled memory, every piece of who she is. The broadcast completes; Voss falls; the ceasefire holds. Emotional beat: grief and release braided together, paying inheritance forward instead of hoarding it.

chapters.title: Lena and the Gravity
chapters.summary: POV Iyo, months later. The ship has landed; Meridian rebuilds under a joint charter. Iyo tends Elodie, who remembers almost nothing but keeps repeating one name—Lena, the sister whose memory she carried longest. Iyo begins recording Elodie's fragments into the new colony archive. Emotional beat: quiet hope; memory survives even when the rememberer cannot.
